entry.title: Omdia Reports Global Tablet Shipments Fell 23 Percent in Q3 2026
entry.content:
Links: omdia.tech.informa.com

Global tablet shipments dropped 23% year over year to 32 million units in the third quarter of 2026, reaching their lowest level in nearly three years, according to research from Omdia. The downturn was led by sharp contractions in the Middle East, China, and Western Europe, driven by persistent supply constraints and waning strategic priority from hardware vendors.

Apple and Samsung retained the top two spots in market share despite significant shipment declines of 28% and 22%, respectively. Lenovo was the sole top-five vendor to achieve growth, increasing shipments by 12% to capture a 12.7% market share, while Xiaomi and Huawei rounded out the top five amid an environment where recent flagship device launches failed to spur broader consumer demand.

entry.content:

Fox Corp. has officially completed its $22 billion acquisition of streaming platform Roku ahead of its previously anticipated 2027 timeline. Roku founder and CEO Anthony Wood will join the Fox board of directors and serve as co-chair of Fox Digital Platforms alongside Paul Cheesbrough, overseeing a newly combined division that includes Roku, Tubi, and other digital assets.

The transaction significantly expands Fox's presence in the free, ad-supported streaming market and digital video advertising space, uniting a platform with over 100 million households with Fox's media assets. Fox stated it intends to maintain Roku as an open ecosystem for the broader streaming industry while expecting to generate about $400 million in annualized cost synergies within two years.

entry.title: Ex-Rockstar Director Obbe Vermeij Says AI Tools Could Accelerate Grand Theft Auto VI PC Ports
entry.content:
Links: arstechnica.com

Former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij warns that emerging AI-powered reverse-engineering tools could enable third parties to port complex console games like Grand Theft Auto VI to PC. He suggests this capability might force developers to narrow the release window between console and PC editions to preempt unauthorized AI-generated ports.

Although converting a massive, highly detailed game via AI would incur significant token costs and produce a product inferior to an official release, Vermeij notes that modern AI coding harnesses permanently alter the security calculus for delayed platform releases. Rockstar has not officially announced a release date for a PC version, though reports indicate it could arrive in early 2027.

entry.title: Jimmy Maher Analyzes the Design and Legacy of Deus Ex
entry.content:
Links: filfre.net | hacker news

Jimmy Maher’s retrospective on Ion Storm’s 2000 role-playing shooter Deus Ex examines both its celebrated status as an immersive sim masterpiece and the cultural hyperbole surrounding its legacy. Drawing on the design lineage of Looking Glass Studios and games like System Shock, the article explores how Deus Ex combined multi-variant problem solving with a traditional linear campaign structure.

The essay highlights the tension between the game's reputation as a prescient work of interactive philosophy and the pragmatic realities of its development. It details behind-the-scenes anecdotes, including Warren Spector's revelation at a 2017 Game Developers Conference postmortem that the protagonist's initials, J.C. Denton, originated from a playfully exasperated exclamation about a helpful friend rather than grand theological symbolism.

entry.content:
Links: salon.com | hacker news

Online news and culture magazine Salon has announced that it is ceasing publication after 31 years, citing the unsustainable business realities of independent digital journalism. Launched in November 1995, the site was an early pioneer of internet publishing, known for its distinct voice combining politics, criticism, and cultural commentary.

The closure marks the end of an influential era for digital media, during which Salon helped shape online journalism and provided a platform for unconventional perspectives. Management expressed gratitude to the founders, journalists, staff, and readers who contributed to the publication's legacy over three decades.
